current.text: Experts see him as a top 35 to 60 player this season. His upside is about top 40. He only reaches top 30 if Paolo Banchero gets hurt.
His main downside this season is his own injury risk.
In auction terms he is worth about 11 to 15 USD. 15 USD is about right.
His draft slot is about round 6. Picks 47 to 49 are a bit early for him.
He is going around picks 54 to 60 in drafts. He has fallen because of injury.
A high ankle sprain and lower minutes hurt his last season.
He is a projected starter next to Suggs, Bane, Banchero and Carter. That group was very good when it played together.
Orlando has a new head coach, Sean Sweeney, so roles may change.
Orlando is projected to win 47 or 48 games and finish as the 6th seed.

durable.text: He has no single standout strength but is good across the board.
He is probably better in category leagues than in points leagues.

He has had two seasons badly hurt by injury. Last season he missed about 47 to 51 games with a high ankle sprain from a contact injury. Before those seasons he was usually reliable and played through ankle rolls.
Phil sees the injuries of the last two years as random, not a chronic problem.

note: Wagner went for 26 USD in our league last season. The market now sits near 8 to 10 USD (Yahoo average cost 10.2 USD, ESPN 8.3 USD), and experts put his value at 11 to 15 USD, so spending above 20 USD means paying for top 30 upside that the experts do not see. He has no weak category (his best are points and FT%, with a projected 84.8% on about 6 attempts), so he fits any build as a steady across-the-board forward. Early in the season, check his ankle and whether his usage holds next to Banchero under new coach Sweeney.
